blocking_finding.title: Two acceptance criteria are arithmetically incompatible, and the shipped denominator class structurally cannot feed the numerator.
blocking_finding.found_by: candidate 2 (grain mismatch) and candidate 3 (no hotlist_id), independently; both driver-verified.
blocking_finding.detail_1_grain: AC-1 requires reproducing 96.6% for Jul 2026 fleet-wide. AC-2 requires the denominator come from DEV-2463's UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery. Those cannot both hold. The ticket's own 96.6% is 11,449 / 11,855 where 11,855 = 'claimed orders (successful, hotlist_id != 0)'. UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery returns {all_claims, successful, deduped} = 15,128 / 14,288 / 11,975 for that window (DEV-2409 comment 38583, screenshot-validated to the unit). 11,855 matches NONE of the three. Reusing 'deduped' yields 11,449 / 11,975 = 95.6%, one full point below the AC's target.
blocking_finding.detail_2_dedup_key: The mismatch is structural, not rounding. UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery.php:107-108 computes deduped as uniqExactIf((forwarder_org_id, agent_org_id, vin), success AND vin != '') -- it dedups on the VIN TRIPLE and DROPS rows with an empty vin. The ticket's denominator dedups on hotlist_id and filters hotlist_id != 0. Different populations on two independent axes.
blocking_finding.detail_3_no_join_key: The string 'hotlist_id' appears ZERO times in app/Clickhouse/Queries/UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery.php (driver-verified by grep -c). Its private sql() selects forwarder_org_id, agent_org_id, vin, success and bucket only. So the class cannot supply the hotlist_id the hits_cold join needs, and 'call it as a black box for the denominator' cannot answer the numerator at any price.
blocking_finding.detail_4_cost: Calling the shipped class for the denominator AND running a separate numerator query means TWO full scans of zod.public_billing_events per cache miss. That table is ORDER BY id with no skip index on ts, event_type or org, so nothing prunes: a 1-month and a 13-month window read byte-identical rows (~38.5M rows / ~1.83GB), and per-org scoping saves nothing (measured 0.00% spread across 11 orgs). The sibling's single-scan query already measures a contended p99 of 9.3s. That directly contradicts AC-4, 'exactly one query per resolved window'.

questions.q: Which denominator -- and therefore which percentage does the card actually show?
questions.answer: OPTION C -- grain-consistent on BOTH sides. Numerator = uniqExact of (forwarder_org_id, agent_org_id, vin) triples whose claimed order had at least one PRE-CLAIM hit in clarity.hits_cold. Denominator = UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery's EXISTING `deduped` stage, unchanged. Fleet-wide Jul 2026: 11,573 / 11,975 = 96.6%. This satisfies AC-1 (reproduces 96.6%) AND AC-2 (denominator comes from the shipped class, untouched) with NEITHER needing amendment, and it is mathematically incapable of exceeding 100%. Supersedes the operator's earlier choice of option B (orders/deduped, 95.6%), which measurement showed would render above 100% for 16 of 257 orgs, worst at 200%.
questions.why_material: AC-1 (reproduce 96.6%) and AC-2 (reuse the shipped query) are arithmetically incompatible; see blocking_finding. This is a sharper question than the ticket's own 'Still open #1', which framed it as 96.6% vs 94.4%.
questions.already_settled_part: Oscar answered the SHAPE on 2026-09-09 (DEV-2409 comment 39274 'option 1 is fine' -- option 1 of comment 39126 was the 96.6% RATE -- plus 39276 giving the formula). Dalton then told Oscar in 39291 'building it as the rate ... the card will read 96.6% for July'. So: a rate, not a volume, and not the 9.97x reading. Settled. What is NOT settled is which claimed-order population divides it.
options: A -- hotlist_id-grained denominator (11,855): reproduces the AC's 96.6% exactly, but the denominator is a NEW population computed inside the new query, so AC-2's 'comes from UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery' becomes false as written and the ticket needs amending.
B -- reuse the shipped 'deduped' stage (11,975): honours AC-2 literally and keeps one grid-consistent claim count across the epic, but the card reads 95.6% and AC-1's 96.6% needs amending.

questions.q: Should 'before the claim' be bounded, or does any sighting in the vehicle's history count?
questions.answer: Ship UNBOUNDED -- any pre-claim sighting counts, however old. Matches the fallback already offered to Oscar in DEV-2409 comment 39291. Record as an explicit caveat on the PR and Build Record. The driver still measures the cost of having no date floor on the hits_cold side at the perf gate, and returns to the operator only if it is unaffordable.
questions.why_material: UNANIMOUS across all 4 candidates that no code answers this. hotlist.lookback_days is real (int, default 270) but appears in app/ ONLY as a model property (Hotlist.php:41, Recoveries.php:28, RecoveriesKitUserScansReport.php:39,266) with ZERO query-time use anywhere in app/Clickhouse/. Per okf/concepts/lpr-assist.md:77 it governs only the Postgres find_historicals() trigger's H/Z historical-hit insertion and is explicitly 'not the assist attribution window'; it never applied to L/S live hits. Using it here would be a NEW use of the field, not reuse of a pattern.
questions.performance_dimension: Candidate 2's finding, and it upgrades this from a business rule to a cost driver: with no lower bound the hits_cold side of the join has no date floor, so it cannot be partition-pruned to the claim's own month and must consider every prior partition for each hotlist_id in the window. hits_cold is PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(hit_created_at) and its sort key is led by hotlist_org_id -- hotlist_id is only a minmax secondary index, so the join key itself prunes poorly.
questions.declared_fallback: Dalton already told Oscar the fallback in DEV-2409 comment 39291: 'If you have no strong view, say so and I'll ship it unbounded and we can tighten it later.' Oscar has not replied to that comment.

questions.q: One SQL statement computing both halves, or two round trips?
questions.answer: EXTEND app/Clickhouse/Queries/UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery.php to expose hotlist_id, so the numerator's hits_cold join and the existing deduped denominator come from ONE shared pass over the claim CTE -- one round trip, no re-port, no second 1.83GB scan. Constraints the driver imposes on itself: the change must be strictly ADDITIVE (window() and monthlySeries() keep their existing {all_claims, successful, deduped} shape byte-for-byte, since DEV-2463 is QA-Complete and merged in #392), and DEV-2463's shipped tests must be re-run and pass unmodified.
questions.found_by: candidates 1, 2 and 3 independently -- NOT in the ticket.
questions.why_material: See blocking_finding detail_3 and detail_4. Two named resolutions, both with real cost: (a) one new self-contained query computing denominator and numerator in a single pass -- satisfies AC-4 and avoids the second 1.83GB scan, but re-derives the claim filter and so reads as the 're-port' AC-2 forbids; or (b) extend the shipped UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery with a hotlist_id-bearing method sharing its CTEs -- one round trip and no duplication, but it modifies a QA-Complete, already-merged class (#392) from another ticket, which the inherited-decisions block never authorised, and would require re-verifying DEV-2463's shipped tests.
questions.precedent: Candidate 3 surfaced that sibling DEV-2464 (Unique Scans to Repo, still on HOLD/unmerged) independently hit the same hazard, recorded on that ticket as 'my port triple-scans billing_events'.

questions.q: Does a hit's hotlist_org_id always agree with the org axis the claim was scoped to, so the hits_cold side needs no separate org filter?
questions.answer: YES -- include hotlist_org_id on the hits_cold side. Measured per-org (largest Jul-2026 claim org) against production: WITHOUT it read_rows=106,717,052 / 3,809.9 MiB / 3,855 ms wall; WITH it read_rows=96,341,520 / 3,777.0 MiB / 1,256 ms wall. Both returned IDENTICAL results (numerator 7,005 / denominator 7,230), so the predicate is result-neutral -- it is a pure prune win plus tenant correctness. hotlist_org_id is hits_cold's LEADING sort-key column; hotlist_id carries only a minmax secondary index. HONEST CAVEAT: the ~3x wall-clock gap is partly page-cache warming (variant A ran first), so the reliable cache-independent signal is the 9.7% read_rows reduction, not the 3x. Read BYTES barely move (-0.9%) because the ~3.8 GiB is dominated by the unprunable zod.public_billing_events, not by hits_cold.
questions.why_material: Correctness AND cost. hits_cold's sort key is (hotlist_org_id, toYYYYMM(hit_created_at), hit_created_at, id); filtering on hotlist_org_id is the only real prune axis, and it is also needed for tenant correctness. Candidate 2 notes it is plausible from Hotlist.php's org_id docblock ('Owning repo Organization') that hotlist_id alone already implies the org, but this was not confirmed against production. Verify with EXPLAIN / X-ClickHouse-Summary at build time rather than assuming.

questions.q: Can the card render MORE than 100% for a single org, given the operator's chosen grain mismatch?
questions.answer: YES for the chosen option B. 16 of 257 orgs (6.2%) would render above 100%, the worst at 200%, on an org-scoped card. Option A and option C are both mathematically incapable of exceeding 100%. Re-raised to the operator with option C, which had not been measured when B was chosen.
questions.why_material: A DIRECT consequence of the Q1 decision, and the driver raised it rather than discovering it in production. The measurement showed 82 (forwarder, agent, vin) triples each span TWO different hotlist orders. Where both of those orders have a pre-claim hit, the numerator gains 2 while the denominator gains only 1. The card is ORG-SCOPED, so fleet-wide masking (95.6%) does not protect a small org: an org whose claims are concentrated in those 82 cases can compute a rate above 100%. Must be measured per-org before planning; if real, the design needs an explicit clamp or the operator needs to revisit Q1.

notes: CRITICAL BUILD CONSTRAINT -- ClickHouse LEFT JOIN default-fill: join_use_nulls defaults to 0, so a LEFT JOIN miss fills non-Nullable scanned_at with 1970-01-01, not NULL. The naive predicate `first_scan < claim_ts` therefore counts every order with NO hit as pre-claim, inflating the card from 96.6% to 99.7% -- silently, and by including exactly the orders the metric excludes. The numerator MUST guard the join miss explicitly (h.hotlist_id != 0, or join_use_nulls=1, or an EXISTS/semi-join). Measured: naive 11,819 vs correct 11,449, the difference being exactly the 370 orders with no hit at all.

CHOSEN SHAPE (option C): numerator and denominator are BOTH counted on the (forwarder_org_id, agent_org_id, vin) triple. The numerator additionally requires the triple's order to have >=1 clarity.hits_cold row with scanned_at < the claim's own epoch ts, with the LEFT-JOIN-miss guard above. The denominator is the untouched `deduped` stage. Measured fleet-wide Jul 2026: 11,573 / 11,975 = 96.6%, zero orgs above 100%.

UNANIMOUS: the new query must PROPAGATE Throwable, not swallow it -- matching UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery. A genuine zero is a normal reading for ~83% of orgs, so a swallowed failure would be indistinguishable from real data. Consequence, per okf/concepts/company-metrics-dashboard.md's blast-radius table: a ClickHouse failure on this card 500s the ENTIRE 16-card grid, in dev and in production. unique-lpr-case-claims is already in that set. This is a deliberate, pre-existing house pattern -- NOT a new risk from this ticket -- but it is easy for a build session to 'improve' with a try/catch that actually makes things worse.

zod.public_billing_events is the ONLY zod.public_* mirror on a ONE-argument ReplacingMergeTree(_peerdb_version). FINAL deduplicates but does NOT drop _peerdb_is_deleted=1 tombstones on this table (PG-028), so an explicit WHERE _peerdb_is_deleted = 0 is mandatory and NOT interchangeable with FINAL.
zod.public_orgs must be read FINAL for the insightlpr-exclusion join or a renamed org fans out 2x and corrupts the count (UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery's own docblock).

NEVER filter titlemax in the counting path -- it is a display flag; only rejectInternalOrgs() (needle 'insightlpr') removes rows. Getting this backwards is a -2.6% error and is precisely what caused the DEV-2409 investigation.
Read hits_cold, never hits_hot: its ~90-day TTL would silently truncate, and 'pre-claim' can span years.

Reconciles exactly: 11855 + 202 - 82 = 11975.
derivation_log.why: Identify WHICH dedup component drives the gap. RESULT: agent_org_id is the ONLY varying component -- vin never varies within an order and forwarder never varies. 201 orders were claimed by more than one repo agency (+202 triples), and 82 (agency, vin) pairs span two different hotlist orders (-82). Establishes that 11449/11975 divides ORDERS by (agency,vin) PAIRS -- a malformed ratio, not merely a different one.

derivation_log.query_shape: oc(claim orders, min(ts)) LEFT JOIN h(SELECT hotlist_id, min(scanned_at) FROM clarity.hits_cold WHERE _peerdb_is_deleted=0 AND hotlist_id IN (...) GROUP BY hotlist_id); compared uniqExactIf(order, h.hotlist_id != 0) against uniqExactIf(order, h.first_scan < claim_ts)
derivation_log.aggregate_result: denom_orders=11855 (matches ticket); orders_with_ANY_hit=11485 (matches ticket EXACTLY); total_hits uniqExact=135119 vs ticket 135008 (append drift); orders_with_PRE_claim_hit computed NAIVELY=11819 -- which is IMPOSSIBLE, being greater than the 11485 that have any hit at all. 11819 - 370 = 11449 and 11855 - 11485 = 370.
derivation_log.why: CRITICAL BUILD FINDING -- the ClickHouse LEFT JOIN default-fill trap. join_use_nulls defaults to 0, so a LEFT JOIN miss fills the non-Nullable DateTime scanned_at with 1970-01-01 rather than NULL. 1970-01-01 is earlier than every claim timestamp, so the naive predicate (first_scan < claim_ts) counts EVERY order with NO hit at all as 'seen before the claim'. That inflates the card from 96.6% to 99.7% by including precisely the orders the metric exists to exclude, and it fails silently. The guard is an explicit h.hotlist_id != 0 (or join_use_nulls=1, or an EXISTS/semi-join). This also PROVES the ticket's 11,449 / 96.6% is correct and reproducible.

derivation_log.why: The RN2 fix dropped h's prune to eliminate the third `kept` expansion, and the driver suspected a net loss. MEASUREMENT CONTRADICTED THE DRIVER: the unpruned shape reads 40.3M FEWER rows and 1,745 MiB FEWER bytes, because removing a full billing_events expansion (~1.83 GB on a table that prunes on nothing) saves more than the unpruned hits_cold aggregation costs. The price is 2.25x peak memory (929.6 vs 412.8 MiB) from the larger LEFT JOIN hash table. Read volume is the dominant cost axis on this table, so the fix is correct and the driver's assumption was wrong.

derivation_log.query_shape: 4 CONCURRENT copies of the shipped window query, read-only against production, wall clock per copy
derivation_log.aggregate_result: 1,572 / 2,918 / 3,204 / 6,373 ms -- contended max 6.4s, against a 5.1s uncontended baseline.
derivation_log.why: R2 -- size COLD_BLOCK_SECONDS against a MEASURED contended figure rather than a scaled guess. Lane 1 projected ~28s by scaling the sibling's 9.3s p99 linearly from read volume; the real 4-way contended max is 6.4s, roughly 1.9x inside the existing 12s block window. So COLD_BLOCK_SECONDS = 12 is ADEQUATE and R2 resolves without a code change to the constant -- only the docblock needed correcting, since it had admitted the value was 'reused as-is regardless'. HONEST LIMIT: measured at 4-way (the DEV-2466 methodology), NOT at the ~29-entitled-org worst case; recorded in the docblock.

derivation_log.param_classes: fixed Jul-2026 UTC bounds as integer epoch; fleet-wide
derivation_log.aggregate_result: denominator 11,975 / numerator 11,573 / rate 96.6% -- unchanged across every shape tried this ticket. Cost: read_rows=107,321,250, read_bytes=3,864.1 MiB, PEAK MEMORY=235.0 MiB, wall 1,035 ms.
derivation_log.why: Confirm the S1+S4 combination delivers what the pre-fix measurement projected. It does: read volume is unchanged versus the previous shipped shape (107.3M vs 106.8M rows) while peak memory drops 4.0x (929.6 -> 235.0 MiB), taking the 29-entitled-org concurrency projection from ~25.1 GB to ~6.7 GB. That is the single risk all three review rounds circled, and it is now the cheap axis rather than the fatal one. NOTE a harness bug worth recording: the driver's first attempt at this query aliased the aggregate AS pre_claim, so ClickHouse resolved a later reference to that UInt64 output instead of the flagged column and raised ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT. The shipped code is immune because it isolates the aggregate in its own `pre` CTE -- the bug was in the ad-hoc measurement, not the code.

derivation_log.aggregate_result: 13 months, total_deduped=129,520, total_pre_claim=125,826. Cost: read_rows=107,398,461, read_bytes=7,225.7 MiB, PEAK MEMORY=260.5 MiB, wall 1,418 ms. 29-way peak projection ~7.4 GB.
derivation_log.why: RN4 lane 2 correctly observed that EVERY cost measurement taken on this ticket was the one-month WINDOW shape, while the 13-month BUCKETED variant runs on 100% of renders (this_month is the default filter and chartSeries() calls getMonthlyData() unconditionally). Measured: peak memory is 260.5 MiB against the window shape's 235.0 MiB -- only 1.11x, so the ~6.7 GB 29-way projection becomes ~7.4 GB. read_bytes roughly doubles (7,225.7 vs 3,864.1 MiB) at near-identical read_rows, i.e. wider granule reads from the larger hits_cold IN-list. CONCLUSION: the gap lane 2 identified was real and worth closing, and the answer is that it does not change the risk verdict.
